options.text: Installing software on a single local computer
Buying servers and housing them in your own datacenter
A private network that links branch offices
Delivery of computing services such as servers, storage, databases and software over the internet, usually pay-as-you-go

explanation: Cloud computing means using a provider's services over the internet instead of owning the hardware yourself.

why_wrong.a: Local installation is not cloud computing.
why_wrong.c: That describes a wide-area network, not cloud computing.

prompt: Under the shared responsibility model, which item is ALWAYS the cloud provider's responsibility?

options.text: The devices people use to connect
The physical datacenter
User accounts and identities
The data you store

explanation: The physical datacenter, physical network and physical hosts always belong to the provider.

why_wrong.d: Your data is always your responsibility.
why_wrong.c: Accounts and identities are always your responsibility.

prompt: A company runs its own Windows virtual machines in Azure (infrastructure as a service). Who is responsible for applying updates to the guest operating system?

options.text: Microsoft and the company equally
The company's internet provider
The company
Microsoft

explanation: With virtual machines you manage the guest operating system, including patching it.

why_wrong.d: Microsoft maintains the hosts and hardware, not the operating system you install in your VM.
why_wrong.a: The split follows the service type, not an equal share.
why_wrong.b: An internet provider has no role in patching your virtual machine.

prompt: A bank must keep customer records on hardware it controls for regulatory reasons, but wants to run its public website in the cloud. Which model fits?

options.text: Public cloud only
Hybrid cloud
Serverless cloud
Private cloud only

explanation: Hybrid cloud combines on-premises or private resources with public cloud services.

why_wrong.a: Public only would move the records off hardware the bank controls.
why_wrong.d: Private only would give up the cloud for the website.
why_wrong.c: Serverless is a way of running code, not a cloud model.

prompt: Which statement describes a public cloud?

options.text: Infrastructure owned by a provider, shared by many customers and reached over the internet
A datacenter located only on a company's premises
A mix of on-premises and cloud resources
Infrastructure used by a single organisation

explanation: Public cloud is provider-owned infrastructure shared by many customers.

why_wrong.b: An on-premises datacenter is not a public cloud.

prompt: Which TWO statements describe the consumption-based model? (Select two.)

options.text: Your costs can never change
You pay for the resources you use
You pay a fixed fee whatever you use
You must buy servers before you can start
You avoid large upfront hardware purchases

explanation: Consumption-based pricing charges for use and removes the upfront hardware cost.

why_wrong.c: A fixed fee regardless of use is not consumption-based.
why_wrong.d: Buying servers first is the traditional on-premises approach.
why_wrong.a: Costs change with usage in this model.

prompt: What usually happens to spending when an organisation moves from its own datacenter to Azure?

options.text: Spending shifts from CapEx towards OpEx
Both CapEx and OpEx rise to the same level
Spending stops completely
Spending shifts from OpEx towards CapEx

explanation: Cloud replaces large upfront equipment purchases (CapEx) with ongoing usage costs (OpEx).

why_wrong.b: There is no reason for both to rise equally.
why_wrong.c: Cloud services are still paid for.

options.text: Developers do not manage servers; the provider runs the code on demand and bills per execution
You must provision virtual machines before running code
No servers exist anywhere
You pay a fixed fee even when nothing runs

explanation: Serverless hides server management and scales automatically, charging for what runs.

why_wrong.c: Servers exist; you just do not manage them.
why_wrong.b: You do not provision machines in serverless.
why_wrong.d: Serverless typically bills for execution, not idle time.

prompt: Which TWO are benefits of a hybrid cloud? (Select two.)

options.text: All on-premises hardware must be removed on day one
Sensitive data can stay on-premises while other workloads use the cloud
Workloads can move to the cloud gradually
The two environments never need a network connection
Security policies are no longer needed

explanation: Hybrid cloud lets you keep what must stay in-house and migrate step by step.

why_wrong.a: Hybrid keeps some on-premises resources, so nothing forces removal on day one.
why_wrong.d: Hybrid environments are connected so they can work together.

prompt: Decide whether each statement about shared responsibility is true.

options.text: The cloud provider is always responsible for a customer's data.
Physical security of the datacenter is the provider's responsibility.
Who is responsible for the operating system depends on the service type.

explanation: Data is always the customer's, the datacenter is always the provider's, and the middle layers depend on the service type.

why_wrong.s1: No. Data is always the customer's responsibility.
why_wrong.s2: Yes. Physical security belongs to the provider.
why_wrong.s3: Yes. IaaS, PaaS and SaaS divide the layers differently.

prompt: Decide whether each statement about cloud models is true.

options.text: A private cloud can be hosted in an organisation's own datacenter.
In a public cloud, the hardware is dedicated to a single organisation.
A hybrid cloud combines public cloud with private or on-premises resources.

explanation: Private clouds can be on-premises, public clouds are shared, and hybrid mixes the two.

why_wrong.s1: Yes. A private cloud can sit in your own datacenter.
why_wrong.s2: No. Public cloud hardware is shared by many customers.
why_wrong.s3: Yes. That is the definition of hybrid.

prompt: Decide whether each statement about cloud pricing is true.

options.text: Pay-as-you-go pricing requires a long-term commitment.
Committing to a reservation or savings plan can lower the price in exchange for the commitment.
Serverless services can scale automatically with demand.

explanation: Pay-as-you-go has no commitment, commitments give discounts, and serverless scales automatically.

why_wrong.s1: No. Pay-as-you-go needs no long-term commitment.
why_wrong.s2: Yes. A one- or three-year commitment lowers the price.
why_wrong.s3: Yes. Serverless scales with demand without you managing servers.

options.text: A private cloud in a single datacenter
An environment that uses two or more public cloud providers
A mix of one public cloud and an on-premises datacenter
One provider's services spread across several regions

explanation: Multicloud means using more than one public cloud provider, and managing resources and security in each.

why_wrong.d: Several regions of one provider is still a single provider.

prompt: A company runs VMware workloads in a private environment and wants to run them in Azure with little change. Which service fits?

options.text: Azure Functions
Azure Arc
Azure DNS
Azure VMware Solution

explanation: Azure VMware Solution runs VMware workloads in Azure.

why_wrong.b: Azure Arc manages resources where they are; it does not run VMware workloads in Azure.

prompt: Decide whether each statement is true.

options.text: In a multicloud environment you manage resources and security in each provider's environment.
Azure Arc can help manage environments that include resources outside Azure.
Multicloud means combining one public cloud with an on-premises datacenter.

explanation: Multicloud involves several public providers, and Arc extends management across hybrid and multicloud estates.

why_wrong.s1: Yes. Each provider has its own environment to manage.
why_wrong.s2: Yes. That is the purpose of Azure Arc.
why_wrong.s3: No. That describes a hybrid cloud.
